question_text: Fill in: 'The government is committed ___ providing quality public service.'

hint_ladder.title: Orient: Spot the Adjective
hint_ladder.text: The blank follows 'committed', an adjective. Know that adjectives often have fixed partners: prepositions they always appear with.

hint_ladder.title: Rule: 'Committed' + 'to' Always
hint_ladder.text: In English, the adjective 'committed' is always followed by the preposition 'to'. Think of them as a pair: 'committed to' is a single chunk.

hint_ladder.title: Apply: Test the Options
hint_ladder.text: Try each: 'committed on providing', 'committed in providing', 'committed for providing'. Only 'to' sounds natural. Say it aloud: 'committed to prov...

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away: The 'Jowa' Mnemonic
hint_ladder.text: Alala mo: 'committed' at 'to' ay parang mag-jowa—hindi sila naghihiwalay. Sa exam, kapag nakita mo 'committed', isipin mo agad 'to'.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you confused 'committed' with 'focused on', but 'committed' always pairs with 'to'.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'involved in' sounds familiar, but 'committed' demands 'to', not 'in'.

C.text: Correct. 'Committed to' is the standard English pairing; it means being dedicated to something.

D.text: You might have chosen D because of phrases like 'committed for trial', but with a gerund, 'to' is the only correct preposition.

next_time_rule: Committed' + 'to' = tamang tandem. Isipin mong kambal sila: hindi puwedeng hiwalay. Kabisaduhin ito bilang isang unit para hindi magkamali.
deconstruct_text:
Let's use a real-life scenario: Your barangay captain is committed to building a new health center. The phrase is 'committed to building'. 'Committed' is like a best friend that always hangs out with 'to'. So kabisado: 'committed to' always.

When you see 'committed', tapos may verb na -ing, automatic 'to' dapat 'yan. Think of 'committed to serving', 'committed to providing'. Other prepositions feel awkward—'committed on' parang hindi maganda sa tenga.

Try saying the other choices: 'committed on providing', 'committed in providing', 'committed for providing'. Lahat sila, parang mali ang tono. Your ear knows the natural pair: 'committed to'. Trust your instinct.

Mnemonic: Isipin mo 'committed' at 'to' ay parang mag-jowa na laging magkasama. Hindi sila naghihiwalay. So whenever you see 'committed', the first word that comes to mind is 'to'.
